A simpler reproduce scenario (to have it exactly corresponding to the linked scenario without Angular): https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-jmk9kp

I can confirm that it looks like a valid bug in Angular template parser. Thnx for reporting!

Thanks! i have more importance to angular component inside svg:foreignObject not displayed.
following is the reproduce link of this in simple version.
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-issue-repro2-8v1ovo

> svg:foreignObject not displayed following is the reproduce link of this in simple version.

@vraddy we are confusing the conversation here a bit by discussing 2 separate issues, I'm afraid. So, the problem that you are raising here is that Angular will create a HTML element corresponding to a component (`<svg-test>` in your example) that we call host element. The issue is that `<svg-test>` is not a valid element that can be used with SVGs hence a browser doesn't render it. This is a well known issue with SVG support in Angular. It can be worked around by using an attribute selector for a component:
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-issue-repro2-kmk65j?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts

To sum, we've got 2 problems here:
* Angular creating host element that doesn't play nice with SVG use-cases
* Angular template parser bug when ones put a `<div>` inside `<foreignObject>`. Reproduction:  https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-jmk9kp

Sorry to put two issues in one thread @pkozlowski-opensource , 
my actual issue was host component was not rendering inside svg:foreignObject(since i was not aware of svg support in angular only as attribute, i was trying to do it in foreignObject as element) from your example it is clear now.. i can get this working by attribute selector, problem solved!

about the div inside foreignObject, this is not my actual issue, since host component was not rendered inside foreignObject, i was trying to experiment with HTML element and caught this comparison working in HTML page and not working in angular project given that information as extra in bug report.

To sum:
Angular creating host element that doesn't play nice with SVG use-cases - attribute component works, solved for me!
Angular template parser bug when ones put a div inside foreignObject - I don't have any use case of this, it was extra information for bug report.

Thanks!

issue.body:
The HTML parser gets an element's namespace either from the tag name (e.g. `<svg:rect>`) or from its parent element `<svg><rect></svg>`) which breaks down when an element is inside of an SVG `foreignElement`, because foreign elements allow nodes from a different namespace to be inserted into an SVG.

These changes add another flag to the tag definitions which tells child nodes whether to try to inherit their namespaces from their parents. It also adds a definition for `foreignObject` with the new flag, allowing elements placed inside it to infer their namespaces instead.

Fixes #37218.
